sources.headline: Zelensky urges US and Musk to lift Starlink restrictions and be on 'right side of history'
sources.text: Ukraine uses the normal Starlink service for communications on the battlefield, while Starshield is used for the interception of missiles and drones in Ukraine airspace.The issue of speed restrictions was first identified in October. It led to conflicting accounts by both Elon Musk and US President Donald Trump.Musk said the US government was responsible as Starshield was controlled by them, but Trump denied being responsible and said he had told the billionaire owner to "put it back".It appeared to be returning to normal after a week, following which Ukraine said the restrictions were still being implemented.The connection issues coincided with a tense diplomatic stand-off between Zelensky and Trump over Ukrainian strikes on oil infrastructure within Russia.Trump said the strikes on Russian oil refineries, which Kyiv says are crucial to stemming the main revenue source for Moscow's war effort, had pushed global prices higher.On Sunday Zelensky said Ukraine was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones targeting electricity substations because "restrictions on the operating speed of Starshield terminals along the front line and in the temporarily occupied territories are still there"."Our interceptor drones lose connection with their operators at a speed of 161km/h (100mph) and simply cannot catch up with Russian jet-powered 'shaheds'," he posted, referring to the drones that follow an Iranian design.On Friday Zelensky said speed limits of around 100mph had been enforced on the network since Monday, but only in Russian-occupied areas and not the whole of Ukraine."It already has political implications. If you impose restrictions there, you are already partially recognising the temporary occupied territories as not ours," the New York Times reported him as saying.Ukraine has also been beset by a shortage of US-made Patriot interceptors used to defend against Russian missiles - a situation that Russia has exploited to intensify strikes on Ukrainian targets.Overnight and into Sunday morning Russia hit energy infrastructure in Zaporizhzhia and the Sumy, Odesa, Zhytomyr, and Kirovohrad regions, Ukraine said.It also struck railway infrastructure in the Dnipro, Kharkiv, and Zaporizhzhia regions.Scores of people are said to have been hurt in those attacks, as well as two in the Donetsk and Kyiv regions.Two people were killed in an attack on an infrastructure facility in Chernihiv Region's Mena, governor Vyacheslav Chaus said.Multiple strikes were also delivered on energy facilities across the region, he added on Telegram.Ukraine meanwhile said it had carried out strikes on a petrochemical plant and an oil refinery in the central Russian city of Nizhnekamsk."On the night of November 15, units of Ukraine's Defence Forces reached Nizhnekamsk in Tatarstan," the military said on Telegram."Two enterprises that feed the Russian war with raw materials and fuel came under attack."Other Ukrainian strikes killed one person in Taganrog, an industrial port city near the border, regional governor Yuri Slyusar said.In the occupied Luhansk region a lorry driver and an elderly woman were also killed, Leonid Pasechnik, the regional leader installed by Moscow said.Meanwhile Estonia has announced it will shut its border crossing points with Russia from 1 December following a suspected sabotage attack on a defence company.Eight people were detained over an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems.The Estonian authorities say they had been ordered by Russia's GRU military intelligence service to try and carry out the attack. Russia has not commented."Russia must understand that hostile actions against Estonia come with consequences," Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said.

Ukrainian military operations were disrupted again this week along the front lines because of restrictions on Starshield, the satellite internet system developed by Elon Musk’s SpaceX and controlled by the U.S. government, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Friday.Mr. Zelensky told reporters that speed limits of about 100 miles per hour were being enforced for Ukrainian devices connected to the system. It would be the second time in recent weeks that Ukraine’s Starshield connectivity had been throttled. The previous restrictions caused Ukrainian drones to lose their connection to the system if they flew above certain speeds.Mr. Zelensky said that the latest speed limits took effect on Monday and were being enforced over Russian-occupied territories, not over all of Ukraine. That hurts Ukraine’s ability to strike Russian troops with drones in those territories.Imposing restrictions on occupied territories is “very dangerous, because it already has political implications,” Mr. Zelensky said. “If you impose restrictions there, you are already partially recognizing the temporarily occupied territories as not ours,” he added.Mr. Zelensky said separately in his nightly speech that the Starshield limits hurt Ukraine’s ability to use newly developed interceptors to protect its cities from Russia’s jet-powered drones. It is likely, however, that those limits would not affect interceptors in Kyiv, the capital, which is being battered by jet-powered drones but is far from the front lines.Mr. Musk and SpaceX did not respond to requests for comment on Friday evening. SpaceX had earlier told Axios that the Ukrainian claim about throttled connectivity was false.Thank you for your patience while we verify access. sources.headline: Zelenskyy questions SpaceX over reported Starshield speed restrictions
sources.text:
Published on
15 November 2026 - 8:15 GMT+1
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has reportedly accused Elon Musk's SpaceX of misleading Kyiv over speed restrictions to its Starshield network.
Zelenskyy said on Thursday that Ukrainian forces were facing restrictions to the service, with terminals limited to a maximum speed of 161 kilometres per hour in areas occupied by Vladimir Putin's invading forces.
"The restrictions have now been in place for five days," the Ukrainian leader said in comments released on Saturday and reported by multiple outlets. "They say it is some kind of technical issue. We do not believe that is the case."
The restrictions have been directly affecting Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian jet-powered attack drones, Zelenskyy said in an address at the European Political Community summit in Dublin earlier this week.
"If someone in America is making decisions that basically treat Ukrainian territory as if it is not Ukrainian, then this tells us where things are going," he told the summit.
On Friday, he added that Kyiv had received "no clear explanations" for the curbs.
"I instructed Ukraine’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Minister of Defense to step up contacts with the U.S. Department of State, the Pentagon, and SpaceX to obtain clarification and resolve the situation," he wrote in a post on social media.
Starshield has proved critical to Ukraine's military operations against Russian forces, providing resilient internet and communications over the battlefield.
It came as Zelenskyy said Washington had proposed the idea of Ukraine ceding land to Russia in exchange for NATO membership as efforts to accelerate peace talks continue.
"The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelenskyy told reporters on Friday in comments embargoed until Saturday, per the AFP news agency.
Zelenskyy added that Ukraine was discussing "specific security guarantees" from NATO and the European Union and that he would ask Ukrainians if they accepted the terms should Western nations confirm.
"I have no right to make that decision on my own," he said.

Published: 2:10am, 16 Nov 2026Updated: 4:18am, 16 Nov 2026

Restrictions on Ukraine’s Starshield satellite communications system are hindering its ability to intercept Russian drones, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Sunday.

He warned that limitations on the system, operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, could weaken defences around Ukraine’s energy infrastructure ahead of the winter months, when Moscow has repeatedly targeted the power grid.

Ukraine’s interceptor drones continue to lose contact with their operators when flying faster than 161km/h (100mph) along the front line and over Russian-occupied territory, leaving them unable to catch Russian Shahed drones, Zelensky said.

“We are counting on these restrictions to be lifted,” he wrote on social media. “The protection of lives and Ukrainian energy infrastructure before winter depends on this.

“The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Defense, and the President’s Office have been instructed to work closely with the American side and SpaceX. It is important to be on the right side of history. We need to help Ukraine.”

Zelensky questioned on Saturday whether the problem was technical, saying the restrictions appeared to have been imposed by SpaceX despite earlier assurances from US Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Starshield was more under US government control.

Zelensky said a meeting of Kyiv’s allies, the so-called Coalition of the Willing, was being prepared and was aimed at defining the European position in talks on ending the war with Russia.

He also said a meeting of the Ramstein group - a grouping of countries helping to support Ukraine’s defence - was set for next week and that “it needs to be productive” and “send a strong signal to Russia that Ukraine will not be left without support”.

Elon Musk’s SpaceX operates Starlink. Photo: Reuters

Europe has chosen five countries - France, Britain, Poland, Germany and Italy - to send representatives to future Ukraine talks.

“We are preparing a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing. It is an important meeting, and it could be a historic one,” Zelensky said in his daily evening address, adding: “We can define a 100-per cent strong European position for victory.”

Until now, talks on settling Europe’s worst war since World War II have been held in the Ukraine-Russia-US format, with Moscow wanting to keep the Europeans out of talks.

“The trilateral format of Ukraine-America-Russia must become not just a quadrilateral format, but also significantly stronger,” Zelensky said.

Moscow has pounded Ukraine in the run-up to winter, continuing strikes during two days of talks in Abu Dhabi this week.

Power cuts after Russian strike on energy facility

Meanwhile, a Russian strike on Chornomorsk, a port city in Ukraine’s Odesa region, injured six people and damaged energy infrastructure, regional head Oleh Kiper said on Sunday on Telegram.

The explosion and falling debris also damaged a gas pipeline and nearby residential buildings, while two parked cars caught fire.

The strike hit a facility operated by DTEK Odesa Electric Networks, temporarily leaving about 41,000 customers without power, Kiper said.

Municipal workers walk among damaged buildings at a site of a drone strike in the city of Chornomorsk, Odesa region, Ukraine on Sunday. Photo: AFP

Overnight Russian air strikes on the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia injured another six people, including a two-year-old boy, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said on Sunday.

Russia launched more than 2,300 drones, 1,590 guided aerial bombs and 15 missiles of various types against Ukraine over the past week, Zelensky said.

Ukrainian drone strikes damaged two electrical substations in Russia’s Rostov region, killing a chief engineer, Governor Yuri Slyusar said on Sunday.

Four people were injured when drone debris fell on their cars, Slyusar wrote on social media. A fifth person was wounded when debris struck a “production facility” in the village of Troitskoye, he said.

Ukrainian forces also targeted Russia’s Tatarstan region, officials said. Radmir Belyaev, mayor of Nizhnekamsk, the region’s third-largest city, said a “large-scale and prolonged attack” damaged its industrial zone.

Six people were injured, and heating and hot water supplies were disrupted in parts of the city, he said.

Ukraine’s General Staff said it had hit two sites in Nizhnekamsk: Nizhnekamskneftekhim, one of the largest petrochemical complexes in Europe, and a production site operated by petrochemical company Sibur. An oil refinery in the area was also hit, it said.

Russia’s Defence Ministry said its forces shot down 533 Ukrainian drones overnight across 13 Russian regions, the Russian-annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea, and the Black and Azov seas.

Drones damage Black Sea ships, Romania says

Romanian Prime Minister Luca Niculescu said on Sunday that three commercial vessels in the Black Sea were struck by drones overnight, the latest in a string of attacks that have raised fears of the war spilling over into Nato territory.

“Once again, maritime security in the Black Sea has been threatened,” Niculescu wrote on social media.

Romania’s Ministry of National Defence said a Greek-flagged oil tanker was struck by a drone, sparking a fire that was extinguished by the crew. Two more ships were later struck by drones, and their crews also extinguished fires on board, the ministry said. No casualties were reported and the ministry did not state the origin of the drones.

“These incidents are unacceptable and constitute a violation of international law,” Niculescu said, adding that they “reflect the deteriorating security situation caused by Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine”.

Last month, a string of cargo ships and tankers were struck by aerial or naval drones near the Bulgarian and Romanian coastlines. At least 30 sailors on commercial ships were confirmed dead or reported missing.

“We will continue to take all necessary measures, alongside our Allies, to strengthen security in the Black Sea,” Niculescu said.

“This remains a key priority for the government, in close cooperation with our regional partners and Nato.”

Additional reporting by Agence France-Presse

sources.headline: Putin takes hard line in US talks as Ukraine says Starlink disrupted again
sources.text: Vladimir Putin warned US negotiators that Russia would target any foreign troops deployed to Ukraine, in a series of hardline remarks that came as the Ukrainian military faced renewed disruptions to Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service.During the talks at the Kremlin with the US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on Thursday, the Russian president refused to soften his territorial demands, insisting on full control over four Ukrainian regions that Moscow claims to have annexed.He also ruled out accepting the deployment of foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine, describing such a move as a “continuation of war”.Putin’s comments appeared to severely dampen hopes that a peace deal could be within reach, after Volodymyr Zelenskyy said there was a “window of opportunity” to reach an agreement before the end of 2026.The latest trip to Moscow by Witkoff and Kushner, who have made numerous visits to Russia, was partly aimed at securing European participation in future negotiations, according to two people familiar with the talks.Speaking after the meeting, Witkoff confirmed that European representatives would join the next round of talks. “They’re our partners, and it’s important for them to be involved,” he told reporters as he boarded a plane leaving Moscow.The US envoys will now travel to Dublin, Ireland, where they will meet Zelenskyy and debrief him on the Moscow meeting.Andy Burnham, the British prime minister, said national security adviser Jonathan Powell would join the talks in Berlin.Amid a flurry of diplomatic activity, including the recent talks in Abu Dhabi, the Kremlin appears to have succeeded in reframing negotiations over the war in Ukraine as part of a broader discussion about European security.But Europe is wary of Russian attempts to focus discussions on a European security architecture, while Moscow continues to pound Ukraine with bombs and missiles.The EU foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, told reporters: “We already have a European security architecture in place.” Kallas pointed to the cold war-era Helsinki accords and the Budapest memorandum, which guaranteed the territorial integrity of Ukraine. “The problem is that Russia is not keeping to those agreements, so right now the focus should be that Russia actually keeps to their obligations … and they don’t attack another country again.” Focusing on a European security architecture was a “distraction” without a ceasefire, she added.Both Washington and Moscow have been urging European leaders to appoint a single representative to lead negotiations on their behalf.“Once a representative is appointed, a chief negotiator authorised to speak on Europe’s behalf, there will be a four-way dialogue,” Putin said on Thursday.EU leaders are due to discuss the issue of who speaks for Europe on Friday, but so far have declined to nominate one person to speak for the bloc. One EU official said the EU would be represented by its institutions when issues concerning the union were on the table, but played down any imminent appointment. They said: “Do I expect an agreement on a special representative? My answer is no, I don’t.”Kallas suggested she – as the EU’s high representative for foreign and security policy – should represent the EU in talks, alongside António Costa, the president of the European Council.More than 45 European leaders are meeting in Dublin for the European Political Community summit, a gathering that brings together nearly every country on the continent, apart from the leaders of Belarus and Russia.The French president, Emmanuel Macron, played down the importance of having a single European negotiator, saying “the content determines the format”. “There is no more US support. So there [are] some mediations, fine,” he said, referring to the process led by Kushner and Witkoff. “But at the end of the day we will be the one to define and decide for our future security as Europeans.”The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, said it was first necessary to get Putin to the negotiating table before deciding on a European envoy. Merz said: “It’s not about individuals. What matters is that Putin is prepared to hold talks.”Meanwhile, Zelenskyy accused Musk’s Starlink satellite service of damaging Ukraine’s ability to defend itself against Russian drone attacks, after Ukrainian military officials reported new restrictions on the system.According to Zelenskyy, Starshield, a military version of Starlink funded by the Pentagon, has for several days been subject to speed limits of 100mph (161km/h) along the frontline and in Russian-occupied territory.Similar restrictions last month prompted confusion over who had ordered them, with Musk and the Trump administration pointing fingers at each other before the service was partly restored.The latest restrictions had made it harder for Ukrainian forces to intercept Russia’s increasingly sophisticated jet-powered drones, Zelenskyy said, accusing the service of “helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine”.Kyiv has contacted Washington to seek an explanation for the disruption, which Zelenskyy said appeared to be deliberate rather than a technical fault.

sources.headline: Ukraine says Starshield throttled again as U.S. pushes for a deal
sources.text:
By
Ramy Inocencio
Correspondent
Ramy Inocencio is a CBS News foreign correspondent based in London, covering Europe and the Middle East. He joined the Network in 2019 as CBS News' Asia correspondent, based in Beijing and reporting across the Asia-Pacific, bringing two decades of experience working and traveling between Asia and the United States.
Read Full Bio
November 12, 2026 / 11:56 AM EST
/ CBS News
Add CBS News on Google
As President Trump's senior envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner landed Thursday in a snowy Moscow to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said connection issues with the Starlink satellite network were again affecting his country's ability to defend itself from incoming Russian missiles and drones.Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces using Starshield, the military version of Elon Musk's Starlink network, which was also impacted last month, were again facing a "systemic speed restriction." Ukrainian interceptors, used to shoot down Russian weapons, have been losing their Starshield satellite guidance connection this week if they try to fly faster than about 100 miles per hour. "Unfortunately, our units have been recording significant malfunctions in Starshield's operation over Ukraine's territory for several days now: along the entire front line and in temporarily occupied Ukrainian territory," Zelenskyy said in a social media post. "Ukrainian military personnel have already investigated the circumstances, and these are not random errors but a systemic speed restriction. For us, this primarily means a significant increase in the difficulty of intercepting Russian jet-powered drones."A Ukrainian official confirmed the restrictions to CBS News, saying "the speed limitations as of now are on Ukrainian occupied territories and across the contact line. The contact line is the first line of our defense and the first point for interception of Russian drones. It started gradually 3 days ago and now it's 100%."
Rescuers and Red Cross volunteers carry the body of a woman killed inside her apartment building by a Russian drone strike in Kyiv, Ukraine, Nov. 12, 2026.
Valentyn Ogirenko/REUTERS
Overnight, Russian drones hit an apartment building in Kyiv, killing one woman, according to authorities, while more energy infrastructure was hit in Rivne in Ukraine's northwest, leaving more people in the dark and cold as temperatures fall.Earlier this week, a Russian strike in the Odesa region killed three people, and multiple strikes across the country caused energy grid disruptions. "Starshield services must be restored urgently for Ukraine to keep its soldiers connected, to protect its citizens and to defend its territory," European Commission spokesman Thomas Regnier said at a news conference in Brussels.
Zelenskyy did not blame anyone for Ukrainian forces' latest problems with the Starshield system. However, one Ukrainian source told CBS News they "are certain" that SpaceX implemented the restrictions, as officials in both the U.S. and Ukraine said was the case during last month's outage.People familiar with the matter told CBS News that Elon Musk himself made the decision to reduce Starshield service in Ukraine last month, after multiple conversations with Trump administration officials. As both sides carried on with their daily attacks — Russia said more than 70 Ukrainian drones were intercepted Thursday, including several headed for Moscow — Witkoff and Kushner carried on with their shuttle diplomacy.Their meeting with Putin in Moscow came after the first round of U.S.-brokered talks between the two countries since February concluded on Wednesday with an announcement of plans for a new prisoner exchange and a commitment to keep talking, but nothing to suggest a wider peace deal could be in the offing.
Russian President Vladimir Putin greets U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, President Trump's son-in-law and adviser, at the Kremlin in Moscow, Nov. 12, 2026.
Sputnik/Vyacheslav Prokofiev/Pool/REUTERS
Speaking after the two-day talks, Kushner, who is President Trump's son-in-law and senior adviser, said he wanted European countries to be involved in the peace process, something both Ukraine and its European partners have long pushed for.
Russia, however, accuses America's European NATO allies of being a party to the war Putin launched more than a decade ago, and ramped up significantly with the ongoing full-scale invasion in February 2022. Speaking Wednesday, Kushner said the U.S. envoys would "see if we can get the Europeans added to the format, so we can make this a multilateral format."He said "the only way to get this done is to have them by our side."During the same briefing after the trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, Russia's chief negotiator Vladimir Medinsky made Moscow's position on Europe clear, telling reporters: "We do not really understand what there is to discuss with them, and they haven't offered a single proposal." Major hurdles to a peace deal remain, including Putin's demand for Ukraine to surrender all of its eastern Donbas region — roughly 20% of Ukraine's overall territory — including some areas Russian forces haven't managed to wrest control of by force. He also wants guarantees that European countries will back off from involvement in Ukraine's security going forward, while Kyiv has long sought membership in the NATO alliance. Witkoff and Kushner were set to fly from Moscow to Dublin, Ireland, later Thursday to meet with Zelenskyy for further discussions.Zelenskyy, in Dublin ahead of the U.S. envoys' arrival to attend a European Political Community Summit with fellow leaders, again noted the Starshield restrictions Thursday, and he alleged that "Putin has told people close to him he wants to destroy life in major Ukrainian cities — Kyiv, Dnipro, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Odesa and other cities."
